_comment: CLUSTER 3 -- {C} PIP SUPPLY, the residue after the phase-2 fixes.
Rule DEPLOYED fires and the plan promises 14 blinks. All fourteen run, and Essence Depleter
drains exactly NINE times: opponent 20 -> 11, then nothing. Cloud of Faeries untaps two lands,
the {C}-starved reservation makes exactly one of them colourless, and Eldrazi Displacer's
{2}{C} eats that one every pass -- so the loop's colourless net is ZERO and the drain is fed
only by the board's opening supply. Across the sweep, `loop.net_c <= 0` produced 39 offers and
ZERO wins; `net_c > 0` won 80.9%.
THE RULING WAS TAKEN AND IMPLEMENTED (fix execution, do not narrow display): ApplyBlinkLoop
now swaps in a pip-free outlet out of hand when a {C}-pip sink is live, and the recognizer
sizes the count on the POST-SWAP colourless net. On THIS BOARD PLUS AN EMIEL IN HAND that is
a clean conversion -- 14 blinks / 9 drains / no kill becomes 20 blinks / 20 drains / WIN --
and it is pinned as test/combo_off/edf_co_14_outlet_switch_to_emiel.json.
WHY THIS FIXTURE STILL FAILS. As authored it has no Emiel anywhere: not on the battlefield,
not in hand, and not in the library (the synthetic matrix fills the library with Forests). The
user's own route for exactly this board is rule 4's -- 'you can draw into Emiel and cast it if
you can draw your deck' -- and the draw engine that would find it is cluster C1a/C1b, which is
owned by another agent and not yet fixed. Once the draw route works, the swap this fixture
needs is already in place and will fire on the drawn copy.
So this is no longer an unattributed failure: it is a KNOWN board waiting on one other fix,
and the mechanism it exercises is separately proven green.
